milestones.title: M2 MVP
milestones.description: MVP: every Must requirement except its sit-and-go-specific parts (REQ-002.6, the sit-and-go part of REQ-044.1, REQ-048.5 stay in M3 with sit-and-go), plus Rapid bot pace. Full casino fixed-limit rules (heads-up, cap, all-ins, side pots, showdown order, button movement) proven by a 1,000,000-hand invariant run; Game Config (2-10 players, stakes, game type, line-up presets and per-seat styles); buy-in/rebuy; pause/resume/leave; four bot styles inside their bands with reproducible decisions; complete advice engine (charts for 3 reference sizes, equity, range model, value and implied-odds rules, explanations, grading, golden spots, determinism); hint; full Hand Review; cash Session Report with style stats, healthy ranges and leaks; Statistics trends with filters and target lines; local persistence; Settings basics.

stories.title: Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
stories.context: First story of the project (user asked that language, toolchain and test harness come first). Single language TypeScript (Q-1). Stack per vision: strict TypeScript, Vite, React, Vitest, fast-check, tsx for the Node playtest CLI, Playwright with @axe-core/playwright (axe) for accessibility checks, ESLint + Prettier. Rules engine, bots, advice and statistics live in modules that import no UI or browser-only code and are enforced by a lint rule. Coverage thresholds: line coverage >= 90% for engine/bots/advice/statistics and >= 70% overall. npm scripts: test, e2e, lint, typecheck, build. This story provisions axe so every M1 screen story can meet the global DoD item 'axe reports zero serious or critical violations' [REQ-057.1]. CI is added by E01-S02 immediately after this story; until then the checks are run locally. Actor 'project owner' = the single Learner in the role of the person who builds and maintains the trainer (requirements.md has only the Learner user class).

acs.text: Given a clean checkout after `npm ci`, When `npm test` runs, Then Vitest executes the unit tests and the fast-check property tests and exits 0
Given a clean checkout, When `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` run, Then ESLint with Prettier and `tsc` with `strict: true` report zero errors and both exit 0
Given a source file with a type error, When `npm run typecheck` runs, Then it exits non-zero; Given a file violating an ESLint or Prettier rule, When `npm run lint` runs, Then it exits non-zero

Given a module under the engine, bots, advice or statistics folders that imports React, a DOM API or IndexedDB, When `npm run lint` runs, Then it reports an error naming the forbidden import and exits non-zero
Given line coverage below 90% for the engine, bots, advice or statistics modules, or below 70% overall, When `npm test` runs with coverage, Then it exits non-zero naming the threshold that was missed
Given a clean checkout, When `npm run build` runs, Then Vite writes the deployable static app to `dist/` and exits 0
Given a clean checkout with Playwright browsers installed, When `npm run e2e` runs, Then a smoke test opens the built app in Chromium and in WebKit and both runs pass

Given `npm run e2e`, When the smoke test runs in Chromium and WebKit, Then it also runs an axe scan of the app's start page and passes only with zero serious or critical violations; Given a test page with an injected critical violation (an image without alt text), Then the axe check fails and `npm run e2e` exits non-zero

stories.notes: Golden-spot tests (E07) join `npm test` when they exist; PWA manifest/service worker (E13) extend `npm run build`. Suggested folders: src/engine, src/bots, src/advice, src/stats, src/ui, tools/playtest. Export a shared `expectNoSeriousAxeViolations(page)` helper for screen stories.
stories.want: a strict TypeScript toolchain where every check runs with one command
stories.benefit: every later story can be built and verified the same way locally and in CI

stories.title: Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
stories.context: Built immediately after the toolchain story E01-S01 so that every later story can meet the global DoD item 'CI workflow is green on the story's branch'. GitHub Actions workflow runs lint, typecheck, tests, the build and `npm run e2e` (Playwright plus axe in Chromium and WebKit, REQ-064.4) on every push and pull request; any failing check fails the workflow. The 10,000-hand playtest step is added by E01-S08, the nightly 1,000,000-hand run by E01-S17 and deployment to GitHub Pages by E01-S18. acs.text: Given a push to any branch or a pull request on GitHub, When the workflow triggers, Then it runs `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run e2e` (Playwright and axe tests in Chromium and WebKit)
Given a push in which any one of lint, typecheck, tests or build fails, When the workflow finishes, Then the workflow is reported as failed
Given a push in which all checks pass, When the workflow finishes, Then the workflow is reported as successful
Given a push in which a Playwright or axe test fails in Chromium or in WebKit, When the workflow finishes, Then the workflow is reported as failed

stories.notes: Cache npm dependencies; pin the Node LTS version used locally.
stories.want: every push and pull request checked automatically in GitHub Actions
stories.benefit: a broken change is caught before it reaches main

stories.title: Rank showdown hands by real poker hand rankings
stories.want: showdown hands ranked by standard poker hand rankings
stories.benefit: the right player always wins the pot
stories.context: Hand evaluator: best five-card hand from two hole cards plus five board cards. Categories high to low: straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, high card; A-2-3-4-5 is the lowest straight. Kickers break ties within a category; suits never break ties. Must agree with the reference table of all 7,462 distinct five-card ranks. The evaluator is also used by the advice engine's equity calculation (E07), so speed matters.

acs.text: Given every distinct five-card hand, When each is evaluated, Then the evaluator produces exactly 7,462 rank classes in the same order as the reference table, with categories ordered straight flush > four of a kind > full house > flush > straight > three of a kind > two pair > one pair > high card
Given the straights A-2-3-4-5 and 2-3-4-5-6, When compared, Then A-2-3-4-5 ranks as the lowest straight, below 2-3-4-5-6 and above any three of a kind
Given two hole cards and five board cards, When the hand is evaluated, Then its rank equals the best rank among all 21 five-card combinations of the seven cards
Given two hands with the same pair and different kickers (K-K-A-9-4 vs K-K-Q-9-4), When compared, Then the hand with the higher kicker wins
Given two hands that differ only in suits, When compared, Then they tie

stories.notes: A lookup-table evaluator (Cactus Kev style or perfect-hash) keeps equity simulation fast enough for REQ-055.

stories.title: Compute a hand's equity against opponent hands
stories.want: equity numbers that match exact poker maths
stories.benefit: I can trust the numbers behind every recommendation
stories.context: Equity calculator on top of the E01 hand evaluator: hero's share of the pot (ties counted as split shares) for a hero hand, a board of 0, 3, 4 or 5 cards and one or more opponent hands or ranges. Must be within 1.5 percentage points of exhaustive enumeration for heads-up preflop matchups (e.g. AA vs KK 81.9%, AKs vs QQ 46.2%). For a given input it returns the same number every time; if sampling is used, the sampler is seeded from the input. Range-versus-range and multiway accuracy against an offline reference set is completed in E07-S06.

acs.text: Given AA vs KK and AKs vs QQ preflop, When equity is computed, Then the results are within 1.5 percentage points of 81.9% and 46.2%
Given a stored set of at least 100 heads-up preflop matchups with exact enumeration values, When the equity test suite runs, Then every result is within 1.5 percentage points of its stored value
Given a three-way preflop matchup AA vs KK vs QQ, When equity is computed, Then each hand's equity is within 1.5 percentage points of exhaustive enumeration
Given the same hero hand, board and opponent ranges, When equity is computed twice in one process and once in a fresh process, Then all three results are identical to the last digit
Given an equity input that uses sampling, When the sampler is created, Then its seed is derived only from the input, so no clock or global random source changes the result

stories.notes: Bots (REQ-055.3, bot decision <= 100 ms) and hints (REQ-055.1, <= 1 s) depend on this speed; prefer exact enumeration where cheap and seeded sampling otherwise. Canonicalise inputs (sort cards/combos) before deriving the seed so equal inputs give equal outputs.

stories.title: Deal every hand from a seeded shuffle with a replay code
stories.want: every hand dealt from a fairly shuffled deck identified by a replay code
stories.benefit: dealing is realistic and any hand can be reproduced exactly
stories.context: Standard 52-card deck shuffled with Fisher-Yates driven by a seeded PRNG. The per-hand seed comes from crypto.getRandomValues in the browser and the Node crypto module headlessly; the seed is recorded as the hand's replay code. Same replay code produces the same deck order; full-hand replay (same replay code + seats + stacks + button + actions -> same cards in the same order) is proven in E01-S07 once the hand engine exists. (Hiding the replay code until the hand ends and showing it in Hand Review are E03/E09.)

acs.text: Given any of 10,000 seeds, When a deck is shuffled, Then it contains each of the 52 cards exactly once
Given 100,000 seeded shuffles, When the position of the first card is tabulated, Then a chi-square uniformity test passes at p > 0.01
Given a new hand in the browser, When its seed is drawn, Then the seed comes from crypto.getRandomValues; Given a new hand in Node, Then the seed comes from the Node crypto module
Given the same replay code, When the deck is shuffled twice, Then both decks have identical card order

stories.notes: Use a small, well-known seedable PRNG (e.g. a 128-bit xoshiro/sfc variant) so replay is stable across browsers and Node.

stories.title: Play a complete fixed-limit hand from blinds to showdown
stories.want: each hand to follow the casino fixed-limit sequence from blinds to showdown
stories.benefit: my practice matches a real casino table
stories.context: Pure, seeded engine for 3-10 players (heads-up is E01-S09). Sequence: post blinds, deal two hole cards each, preflop betting, flop (3 cards) and betting, turn (1) and betting, river (1) and betting, showdown; ends early when all but one fold. Small blind = player left of button, big blind = next player. Preflop action starts left of the big blind; later streets start with the first active player left of the button. Bets/raises are one small bet preflop and flop, one big bet turn and river. At $4/$8 blinds are $2/$4. Pot goes to the best hand; tied pots split equally, an odd dollar to the first tied player left of the button. The engine exposes (and an AC verifies) the legal action set with exact amounts for the player to act. Cap, all-ins, side pots, showdown order and button movement come in M2 stories. Money and chips are integers; the odd-unit rule is the same for sit-and-go chips (tested in E01-S13). Interim M1 behaviour (until E01-S10, and until E01-S16 for stacks, in M2): every seat starts each hand with the $160 cash buy-in (20 big bets at $4/$8, REQ-007.1), which exceeds the $96 the most one player can put into a capped hand ($16 preflop + $16 flop + $32 turn + $32 river), so no all-in can arise; and seat policies never make a fifth bet on a street, so the 4-bet cap invariant holds before the engine enforces it.

acs.text: Given 6 players at $4/$8 with the button at seat 1, When a hand starts, Then seat 2 posts the $2 small blind and seat 3 posts the $4 big blind

Given a scripted deck and 6 players with the button at seat 1, When hole cards are dealt, Then cards go one at a time clockwise from seat 2 for two rounds, so seat 2 receives deck cards 1 and 7 and seat 1 receives cards 6 and 12

Given blinds are posted with the button at seat 1, When preflop begins, Then seat 4 acts first; Given the flop, turn or river, When betting begins, Then the first active player left of the button acts first

Given 6 players at $4/$8 with the button at seat 1, When the engine lists legal actions, Then seat 4 preflop gets exactly fold, call $4 and raise to $8, the first player to act on the turn with no bet facing gets exactly check and bet $8, and every bet or raise is exactly $4 preflop and on the flop and exactly $8 on the turn and river
Given a betting round, When every active player has acted and all have put in the same amount, Then the round ends and the next street deals 3 flop cards, then 1 turn card, then 1 river card
Given all players but one have folded, When the last fold is applied, Then the remaining player wins the pot without showing cards and no further cards are dealt

Given river betting has ended with seats 2 and 5 tied for the best hand in a $27 pot with the button at seat 1, When the pot is awarded, Then seat 2 receives $14 and seat 5 receives $13; with the button at seat 3 instead, seat 5 receives $14 and seat 2 receives $13; with one best hand, that player receives the whole $27

Given 100,000 random seeded hands with 3 to 10 players, every seat starting the hand with the $160 buy-in and random legal actions that never make a fifth bet on a street, When each is played, Then every hand terminates in a legal end state (one player left or a completed showdown)

stories.notes: Model the engine as pure functions: applyAction(state, action) -> state, legalActions(state). Keep money as integer dollars/chips.

stories.title: Give each deciding seat only its own view of the hand
stories.want: opponents to decide using only what they could see at the table
stories.benefit: bots never cheat by seeing my cards or the next card
stories.context: The engine passes any deciding code (bots, playtest seat policies, later the advice engine) a PlayerView: own hole cards, the board, all actions and stacks, the legal actions with exact amounts, and cards shown at earlier showdowns; never other players' hole cards or undealt cards. Separation is type-level: decision APIs accept only PlayerView.

acs.text: Given a hand in progress, When the engine asks a seat to act, Then it passes a PlayerView with that seat's hole cards, the board, all actions, all stacks and cards shown at earlier showdowns, and no other player's hole cards or undealt cards
Given a fixed decision point, When the other players' hole cards and the undealt deck are changed, Then the PlayerView is deep-equal to the original and a seeded seat policy returns the same action
Given decision code that is passed the full game state instead of a PlayerView, When `npm run typecheck` runs, Then it reports a type error

stories.notes: Hints and grades using the user's view (REQ-025.2/025.3) are E07.

stories.title: Recommend a preflop action from the 6-max chart
stories.want: a preflop recommendation for my hand taken from an authored 6-max chart
stories.benefit: I learn which starting hands to play from each position
stories.context: Every preflop recommendation comes from authored chart data files loaded by the advice engine (not hard-coded logic). A chart gives, per position and preflop situation, the action for each of the 169 starting-hand classes. Situations per position: unopened pot, facing one or more limpers, facing a raise, facing a raise and calls, facing a re-raise, blind defence. Each cell: one action (fold, call, raise), a borderline flag, zero or one acceptable alternative action. Each chart file carries a plain-English justification of its ranges, written for this project. The advice API accepts only a PlayerView (E01-S06), so hints and grades see only the acting player's view. This slice delivers the 6-max chart; heads-up and full ring follow in E07-S05. The TAG bot (E06) is built on this API. Applicable 6-max (position, situation) pairs (26): unopened pot - UTG, HJ, CO, BTN, SB; facing one or more limpers - HJ, CO, BTN, SB, BB; facing a raise - UTG, HJ, CO, BTN; facing a raise and calls - UTG, HJ, CO, BTN; facing a re-raise - all six; blind defence - SB, BB. The blinds facing a raise (with or without callers) use blind defence.

acs.text: Given the 6-max chart data, When the chart validator runs, Then each of the 26 applicable (position, situation) pairs listed in the context assigns an action to all 169 starting-hand classes, and a missing pair fails validation naming it

Given a chart cell with no action, an action other than fold, call or raise, or more than one acceptable alternative, or a 6-max chart file without a plain-English justification, When the chart validator runs, Then validation fails naming the position, situation and hand class of the bad cell, or the chart missing its justification
Given one chart cell is changed in the data file and no code is changed, When advice is requested for that position, situation and hand class, Then the recommendation follows the edited cell

Given a 6-max PlayerView at a preflop decision, When advice is requested, Then it returns the cell's action, its borderline flag, its acceptable alternative (or none) and the position and situation used
Given a fixed preflop decision point, When the other players' hole cards and the undealt cards are changed, Then the recommendation is identical
Given code that passes the full game state instead of a PlayerView to the advice API, When `npm run typecheck` runs, Then it reports a type error

Given a 6-max preflop decision facing a fourth bet (a re-raise of a re-raise), When advice is requested, Then it uses the facing-a-re-raise chart cell for the hand class, and a raise recommendation becomes call because the street is capped

Given a 6-max big blind with no raise in front of it (one or more limpers) holding a hand class whose facing-limpers cell is call, When advice is requested, Then it returns check, because no bet is facing the big blind

dod.text: Chart ranges and justification text are original, written for this project

stories.notes: Recommendations are always legal for the view: a 'call' cell with nothing to call becomes check (AC8); facing a fourth bet the street is capped (one bet plus three raises, REQ-016.3), so a raise cell becomes call (AC7, REQ-032.6). Heads-up and full-ring fourth-bet checks are in E07-S05.

stories.title: Run seeded bot-only hands from the command line
stories.want: to run seeded bot-only hands of the production engine from the command line
stories.benefit: I can prove the game works without clicking through hands
stories.context: Headless playtest CLI on Node via tsx: `npm run playtest -- --hands <n> --seed <s> --size <players>`; default 6-max $4/$8 cash table. Uses the production engine and PlayerView-based seat policies. The same seed and options must produce identical output. Line-up preset, style checks (REQ-027.5), advice determinism check (REQ-036) and bot BB/100 reporting (REQ-062.3) are added by E06/E07 once bots and advice exist. The runner can replay a recorded hand from its replay code, seats, stacks, button and actions (REQ-013.3). Actor 'project owner' = the single Learner in the role of the person who builds and maintains the trainer (requirements.md has only the Learner user class). Interim M1 behaviour (until E01-S10, and until E01-S16 for stacks, in M2): every seat starts each hand with the $160 cash buy-in (20 big bets at $4/$8, REQ-007.1), which exceeds the $96 the most one player can put into a capped hand ($16 preflop + $16 flop + $32 turn + $32 river), so no all-in can arise; and seat policies never make a fifth bet on a street, so the 4-bet cap invariant holds before the engine enforces it. The runner resets every seat to the $160 buy-in before each hand in M1.

acs.text: Given `npm run playtest -- --hands 10000 --seed 42`, When it runs, Then it plays 10,000 hands at a 6-max $4/$8 table with the production engine, prints a report with hands played and the invariant-violation count, and exits 0
Given `--size n` for each n from 3 to 10, When the playtest runs, Then every hand is dealt to exactly n players
Given the same seed and options, When the playtest is run twice, Then the two outputs are byte-identical
Given seeds 42 and 43 with otherwise identical options, When both runs complete, Then the dealt replay codes differ

Given a hand recorded by a playtest run (replay code, seats, stacks, button and actions), When the hand is replayed through the engine, Then every seat receives the same hole cards and the board shows the same cards in the same order

Given the M1 seeded random-move seat policy and a street that already has 4 bets (bet plus three raises, the big blind counting as the first bet preflop), When the policy chooses an action, Then it chooses only call or fold and never bet or raise, so `npm run playtest -- --hands 10000 --seed 42` records no street with more than 4 bets

stories.notes: Until E06 bots exist, seats use a seeded random-legal-action policy (RNG from replay code + seat) that never makes a fifth bet on a street. Before each hand every seat is reset to the $160 buy-in; from E01-S16 on the runner keeps real stacks and restores only busted cash seats to $160. E06 owns bot replacement for the real app (REQ-007.5).

stories.title: Check game invariants after every playtest action
stories.want: every playtest action checked against the game invariants
stories.benefit: any rules bug is caught with a replayable hand
stories.context: After every action the playtest verifies: chip conservation, legal action, cap respected (at most 4 bets per street), pot eligibility, no card dealt twice. On a violation it prints the replay code and action history and exits non-zero. CI runs a 10,000-hand playtest and fails on a violation. Actor 'project owner' = the single Learner in the role of the person who builds and maintains the trainer (requirements.md has only the Learner user class). In M1 the cap check is satisfiable because seat policies never make a fifth bet and stacks are reset to $160 before each hand (see E01-S07); from E01-S10 the engine itself enforces the cap.

acs.text: Given any action applied in a playtest, When it is checked, Then the runner verifies that stacks plus pots equal the table total, the action was in the legal set, no street has more than 4 bets, every pot's eligible players contributed to it and still hold cards, and no card was dealt twice

Given an injected engine fault for each invariant (chips created, illegal action accepted, fifth bet allowed, ineligible pot winner, duplicate card), When the playtest runs, Then it reports that invariant as violated
Given an invariant violation, When the playtest stops, Then it prints the hand's replay code and full action history and exits non-zero
Given a push to GitHub, When the CI workflow runs, Then it runs a 10,000-hand playtest and the workflow fails if the playtest exits non-zero

stories.notes: Fault injection via a test-only engine wrapper; keep the checker in the engine package so unit tests can reuse it.

stories.title: Recommend call or fold after the flop from equity and pot odds
stories.want: a call-or-fold recommendation after the flop that compares my equity with the pot odds
stories.benefit: I learn when a call is worth its price
stories.context: Postflop method: compute hero's equity against the opponents and the required equity = call amount / pot after calling; recommend call over fold when equity >= required equity. Every postflop recommendation returns the action, equity %, required equity % and the id of the rule that fired. All postflop rules are written in one design document and every rule has a unit test. In this slice opponents' holdings are every unseen two-card combination; the action-based range model (E07-S07) and observed-stat scaling (E07-S09) narrow them later without changing this rule. Value bets (E07-S10) and implied odds (E07-S11) are later rules.

acs.text: Given a flop decision facing a $4 bet with a pot of $20 including that bet (required equity 4 / 24 = 16.7%), When hero's equity equals the required equity, Then advice recommends call
Given the same decision, When hero's equity is 0.1 percentage points below the required equity, Then advice recommends fold
Given any postflop decision, When advice is requested, Then it returns the action, equity % and required equity % to one decimal place and the id of the rule that fired

When the opponent bets, keep Strong, Pair and Draw; checks, keep Pair, Draw and Air; calls a bet, keep Pair and Draw; raises, keep Strong and Draw. Narrowing applies street by street to the range left by the previous street. The model never reads a bot's style label or internal parameters: advice inputs are the PlayerView plus observed opponent statistics only. stories.context: Implied-odds rule (postflop design document): applies only when hero holds a draw (a flush draw counts 9 outs, an open-ended straight draw 8 outs, outs that also improve an opponent's likely better hand are not removed in this rule) and at least one card is still to come. Required equity with implied odds = call amount / (pot after calling + one big bet for each opponent still in the hand), the extra big bet standing for what hero expects to win on a later street when the draw hits. If equity is below the plain required equity (REQ-033.1) but at least the implied required equity, advice recommends call with the implied-odds rule id and lists the outs; otherwise the pot-odds result stands. Rule precedence: value bet/raise (E07-S10), then pot-odds call, then implied-odds call, then fold (or check when free). Worked example at $4/$8 (AC1): hero Ah5h, opponent range {KsQd}, board Kh 8h 7c 2d; 9 heart outs of 44 unseen cards give equity 20.5%.

stories.context: Enabler (no user-visible outcome on its own): pure statistics module (no UI imports) over completed hand action histories. VPIP = hands where the player voluntarily put chips in preflop (call or raise, not counting blinds) / hands dealt. PFR = hands with a preflop raise / hands dealt. W$SD = showdowns where the player won chips / showdowns reached. A zero denominator shows '—'. User stories that show these stats depend on this task: E07-S09 (opponent range scaling), E03 opponent stats panel, E06 style checks and the E10 Session Report.

stories.context: From 30 observed hands of an opponent in the session, that opponent's preflop range width is scaled toward their observed stats by the formula in the range-model design document: width = d + (o - d) x min(n, 100) / 100, where d is the default range's width (% of starting hands), o is the observed PFR for raising ranges or the observed VPIP for calling and limping ranges, and n is the number of observed hands; the range is then the strongest width% of starting hands by the documented hand order, never narrower than the single strongest hand class (AA). Below 30 hands the default range is used. Recommendations state the basis per opponent: 'typical player' or 'based on N hands of this opponent'; the hint (E08) and review (E09) display it.
